title: Iranian Commercial Vessel Struck Near Hengam Island in Strait of Hormuz, One Killed
detail: An Iranian commercial cargo vessel was struck by an unidentified projectile near Hengam Island in the Strait of Hormuz at around 5:00am local time Sunday. Iran's state news agency IRNA named the seafarer killed as Jamshid Rajabi, one of the vessel's 10-member crew; four others were wounded. A fire broke out aboard and local authorities assisted with evacuation. The governor of Qeshm blamed a 'terrorist enemy' but said neither the projectile type nor those responsible had been identified. The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) confirmed a vessel transiting the strait was hit and caught fire, without identifying the attacker.

media.caption: Commercial vessels anchored in the Strait of Hormuz near the site of the Sept 13 strike off Hengam Island

confidenceReason: The strike, casualty count and location are corroborated across Washington Post, CBC and AP citing Iranian state media (IRNA) and UKMTO; the attacker and weapon type remain unidentified by any party.

title: Iraq Seizes Drone-Launching Platform Used in Saudi Pipeline Attack Near Iranian Border
detail: Iraqi security forces located and seized a drone-launching platform in Maysan province's al-Tayeb border district near the Sheeb crossing, east of Amara, that was used to launch the long-range drones -- reported capable of traveling roughly 1,100km -- in the Sept 10 attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline. Lieutenant General Saad Maan said Iraq applies a 'principle of preventive sovereignty' against attacks launched from its territory. Iraq's commander-in-chief approved an Iranian request to join the investigation and review its findings; the article cites no direct evidence of Iranian government involvement, only that the launch site sits in a border region where Iran-aligned militias maintain a presence.

media.caption: Iraqi security forces seize a drone-launching platform in Maysan province near the Iranian border, Sept 13, 2026

confidenceReason: Single-pole (Iraqi official) account reported by Al Jazeera; no independent confirmation of the platform's origin or operators beyond the Iraqi military's own statement.

title: NYT: Iranian Hardliners Staged Unauthorized July Hormuz Attacks That Sank a Near-Complete US-Iran Peace Deal
detail: The New York Times reported that a hardline faction led by cleric Hossein Taeb -- former head of IRGC intelligence and recently appointed to lead the Basij militia -- launched unauthorized attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz in early July without the knowledge of President Pezeshkian, Iran's civilian leadership, or even IRGC chief Gen. Ahmad Vahidi, effectively killing a near-complete US-Iran memorandum of understanding. According to Iranian officials cited in the report, Pezeshkian was 'surprised' by the attacks and angrily called Vahidi, who said he had neither authorized nor known of the strikes beforehand. The revelation triggered what the report called some of the most volatile disagreements among Iran's leaders in recent years, with several officials threatening to resign. The report attributes hardliners' ability to act unilaterally to a leadership vacuum, noting Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has not been seen in public since succeeding his father in March.

media.caption: Report details an internal Iranian leadership rift over unauthorized July Hormuz attacks that derailed a US-Iran peace deal

confidenceReason: Sourced to unnamed Iranian officials via NYT reporting, relayed by Times of Israel and corroborated in broad strokes by Ynetnews; no on-record Iranian government confirmation of the internal account.
